turns.author: danielhstahl
turns.note: The bead decomposition itself: 94 beads created 01:14-01:15 and committed at 01:15. No bead id on the commit and no claim window, so T1 and T2 have nothing to say; it is its own turn, not part of reco-8yk's, which had already released.

turns.author: danielhstahl
turns.note: 4 seconds apart, and the second commit corrects a sentence the first one added, in the same file it added (docs/adr/0005-harness-contract.md §11.1) plus a .gitignore line nobody else touched. One act, two commits: nothing was claimed or released in between. This is the corpus's only seconds-apart pair, and the one the time-gap rule can never see.

turns.author: Fathom Agent
turns.note: The one commit in the corpus whose author identity itself carries agent evidence (`Fathom Agent <agent@example.invalid>`), which is also why it is the only real turn the `author` rule fires on for the right reason rather than by accident.

turns.author: danielhstahl
turns.note: A CI fix that landed 94 s after reco-dsh released and 65 s before reco-f28 was claimed: between two turns, so it belongs to neither. The single-file diff greps the keyprobe's real machine keys in a step written 12 turns earlier by reco-e0e (t09). ADR-003 §8's interleaved case, arrived at by a loop rather than by a person.

turns.author: danielhstahl
turns.note: Two commits, 33.6 minutes apart, one bead, and the only real turn with a closed_by_session on the board, so T1 settles it. The second commit is the operator-facing half of the first (force_split is how e1.3 lets a human disagree with the cascade). The gap rule at its published 30-minute default cuts this turn in half, which is the single most expensive number in the corpus.

turns.author: looprs
turns.note: The first commit the loop authored as itself (`looprs`) rather than under a person's identity.

turns.author: looprs
turns.note: 1.1 minutes after t30's commit and 15 s before reco-bjd was claimed: the loop noticed the harness was dropping session logs into the working tree and excluded them. One line in .gitignore, and every signal Fathom has reads it as part of the turn before it.

pathologies.why: The force_split/force_merge configuration is the half a reviewer has to be able to use; on its own card it is a feature nobody can operate, and the accept given to the first half is recorded against a card that does not contain the operator's escape hatch.
A correction to the document added 4 seconds earlier. Split, the reviewer of the ADR is reading a sentence the same turn had already found wrong, and the wrongness is in a different card.
A turn that changes CI and rides on the previous turn's card inherits that turn's accept/dismiss. Nobody looked at it; the queue would say it had been reviewed.
The only commit that keeps harness session logs out of the index. Absorbed into the turn before it, it is invisible in a product whose premise is that a reviewer can enumerate what changed.

The step it fixes was written 12 turns earlier (t09). The boundary here is correct and must stay: the remedy is the lineage window ADR-001 §5 already defines, not a merged episode. Annotated so the report can state what share of real pathologies segmentation is not able to protect at all.

notes: 34 commits, 32 turns: 30 of the 32 are one commit long, and the two that are not are the only grouping evidence this history contains. That is a property of the loop (it commits once, at the end, then closes the bead), and it is why the report prints the `every commit is its own episode` baseline beside every strategy: on this stratum that trivial rule scores 0.94 boundary F1, and any strategy that beats it by less than a point is not being tested.

Not one commit carries an Agent-Turn / Agent-Session / Fathom-Episode trailer, and no .fathom/events.jsonl exists for any of them, so the `hook` and `trailer` rules have zero evidence to fire on here — which is ADR-003 §9.3's `created_source = index` for every real episode in this repository, stated as a measurement rather than as a table.

The harness's own record (bead claim/release windows) is carried per commit under `harness`, and it is an independent derivation of the same 32 boundaries: 30 commits fall inside exactly one claimed bead, and the remaining four (t02, t04's second commit, t14, t31) fall in a gap between beads, which is exactly the reason each is annotated as its own turn or joined under T3.

`kind` is `unknown` for 25 of 32 turns on purpose: the board's assignee is a person's name even for work an agent did, and the author string is a person's identity for all but five commits. Per ADR-003 §8 H4, no evidence is `unknown` at 0.0, not a guess. Note also that the loop's own identity `looprs` matches none of §4.4's agent markers, so H4 files those four turns as `human` at 0.5 — recorded as a failure mode for `e4.1` (reco-w7q), not silently fixed here.
